Under the natural reading (event.status field == 'confirmed'), ev_demo_target passes and is the sole match. Under a stricter alternate reading (all attendees, including the room resource, have responded 'accepted'), ev_demo_target would also fail, since its room-2b resource attendee shows 'needsAction' - a status that persists indefinitely for rooms in this data. That reading would eliminate the only match, but it's an unnatural way to read 'confirmed' for a meeting and isn't consistent with how calendar room resources normally behave, so it shouldn't be adopted.

Under the natural reading (a room resource attendee is present), ev_demo_target, ev_demo_tentative, and ev_demo_location_link all satisfy this. Under an alternate reading (the event's location text names a room), none of the records qualify, since the only populated location field (on ev_demo_location_link) contains a fake Meet URL, not a room name. This alternate reading would eliminate the intended match, but resource-attendee is the standard/expected signal for 'room booked' in this data model, so it's the reading a colleague would take.
